involved and not for Article ॥4. Finally, we come to the present case. It is not contended before us that any 
fundamental freedom is affected. We need not therefore go into the question of "proportionality". There is no 
contention that the punishment imposed is illegal or vitiated by procedural impropriety. As to "irrationality", there 
is no finding by the Tribunal that the decision is one which no sensible person who weighed the pros and cons 
could have arrived at nor is there a finding, based on material, that the punishment is in "outrageous" defiance of 
logic. Neither Wednesbury nor CCSU tests are satisfied. We have still to explain "Ranjit Thakur (7987 [4] SCC 
644). 


He has further submitted that, the common thread running through in all these decisions is that the Court 
should not interfere with the administrator s decision unless it was illogical or suffers from procedural impropriety or 
was shocking to the conscience of the Court, in the sense that it was in defiance of logic or moral standards. In view 
of what has been stated in the Wednesbury s case (supra) the Court would not go into the correctness of the choice 
made by the administrator open to him and the Court should not substitute its decision to that of the administrator. 
The scope of judicial review is limited to the deficiency in decision -making process and not the decision 


Learned Counsel further submits that only because co-delinquent has been granted lesser punishment, it 
cannot be a ground to interfere in the punishment and has referred to Judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court in the 
case of Chairman and Managing Director, United Commercial Bank Vs. P.C. Kakkar (2003) 4 SCC 364. 


Next submission from the Management is that, the Workman has been previously punished for misconducts. 
This factor also cannot be ignored. 


It has been found that, three of the five charges were wrongly held proved and in fact they are not proved 
in accordance with law. Now remains the charge of active concealment of fact regarding Departmental 
Enquiries/Punishments while submitting Consent Form in 2007 and 2008 for Departmental Examination. This is also 
undisputed that the Workman was permitted to appear in the Departmental examination under order of Hon’ble High 
Court. In my considered view, the maximum punishment of removal from service of a Workman who had putting 
more than 20 years in service of the Bank for these charges is nothing but disproportionate and shocks the conscience 
of this Tribunal. After evaluation material on record, I am of the considered view that the punishment of compulsory 
retirement of the Workman for these charges will be adequate and proportionate to the charges. Punishment order 
requires to be modified accordingly. 

Issue No. 3 and 4 is answered accordingly. 

No other point was pressed. 

On the basis of above discussion and findings, the reference is answered as follows. 

AWARD 

Holding the action of Management of State Bank of India, in imposing the punishment of dismissed 
without notice upon the deceased Workman Balwant Singh Gour vide order dated ३30,04.2070 is unjustified in law, 
the punishment is modified from dismissal without notice to compulsory retirement with benefits.

As per letter dated 7/0/207 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference is 
made to this Tribunal under Section-l0 of Industrial Disputes Act, |947 (in short the ‘Act’)as per Notification 
No. L-40/30/207 (IR(B-D) dt. !7/0/207. The dispute under reference relates to: 


"Whether the action of the Railway Administrative of SEC, Raipur in implementing the Rly Board order 
No. 83 Electric(I) 736/6 dated 24/25.70, 27965 i.r.o. payment of Overtime Allowances to Maintenance- 
cum-Escorting staff deployed in AC Coaches is legal and justified? If not, what relief the workmen 
performing both Maintenance & Escorting jobs are entitled to?" 


After registering the case on the basis of reference, notices were issued to the parties. They appeared and 
filed their respective statement of claim and defense. 


Case of the workman union is mainly that, the Workman Nazir Ahmed was employee of Railway, initially 
appointed on 0.0!.986 on the post of helper and was posted in the Office of Senior Engineer SSEE (AC/LT/Durg) 
under maintenance roster. There are two rosters with respect to AC, one is maintenance and other is escort roster. The 
work/duties and nature of work of two rosters are different, their working roster hours are also different. In the 
maintenance roster, as mentioned in letter of Maintenance dated 2.2.203, where the workman was working as a 
helper, the employee is required to complete 96 hours on duty in I4 days and will be entitled to overtime allowances 
for work above the ceiling limit of 96 hours in 4 days. Likewise, the hours of duties for AC escorting rosters is 04 
hours in l4 days and employee AC escorting rosters becomes entitled to get overtime allowance for the hours he 
worked above the specified limit of l04 hours in l4 days. The Management of Railways issued a letter No. 
E/PB/R/Welfare/TA & OT/0I/204 dated 4.05.20I5 by which the provisions of 04 hours in [4 days for Escort 
Rosters employee was made applicable to the employees in the Maintenance roster also which is without authority, 
unjust, illegal and arbitrary. 


It is further the case of the Union that, the Divisional Electrical Engineer Raipur issued a letter dated 
6.05.20i] in which it was mentioned that no employees/helper of maintenance roster should be provided work in 
AC escorting roster for duties of Escorting AC Coaches and Power coaches. There are separate guidelines vide letter 
No. 83 Elect/(i)l38/8 dated 24/25.0.985, which provide that where ever possible, the break in duty may be 
considered at important en route stations having resting facilities after 0 to 2 hours duty with fresh set of staff 
taking over and where this is not feasible, the staff should be given adequate compensatory rest at home station to 
keep this cumulative duty hours below the permissible limits of !04 hours period. The Union has further alleged that, 
Railway Board letter No. E(LL)74/HER (RLT) I0 dated !3.08.975 further provides in its Clause 9(b) that the 
instructions in his letter shall equally apply to continuous workers under H.O.E.R. of Electrical Department working 
in locomotive Running Sheds. On this score also, the fixing of 04 hours limit for !4 days for maintenance roaster 
staff is without sanction of law. The Union has prayed that direction be issued to the Management of Railways to pay

over time to the Workman Nazir Ahmed for hours above ceiling limits of 96 hours in l4 days which he had spent on 
duty. 


Management has defended its action with the case that as per Railway Provisions Instructions dated 
27.06.985, the AC/Technician, AC Helpers and Khalasi are allowed one hour before commencement of journey for 
completing pre-departure taking over formalities at the out-station also at the end of their outward journey, they are

Railways V.s. Nazir Ahmed and directed the Railways to calculate and pay overtime allowance to the applicants as per 
Rules and Circulars of Railways and has pleaded that the Railway Board Circular was not quashed. It is also the case 
of Railways that Principal Bench of Central Administrative Tribunal at New Delhi dismissed a petition OA No. 
230/2077 holding that no overtime allowance with respect to halt period at a destination station. In this case also, the 
validity of the said circular was not calculated. Hence, the present claim is barred by principle of Res judicata. 


In evidence, the workman Nazir Ahmed has filed his affidavit as his examination in chief. He has been 
cross-examined by Management of Railways. Railways have filed affidavit of its witness Khilawan Singh Kanwar,

has further filed and proved documents which are information obtained from RTI dated 3.0.202] relating to copies 
of Overtime Vouchers, total roster duty hours, actual hours of duty performed by employee Roop Singh and extra 
duty hours, as well reasons for working extra hours with relation to employees Roop Singh, Akash Shrivastava, Dauli 
Chand Sharma and many others who have been working with Western Central Railway as AC Mechanics, 
Technicians/fitter/helper to show that they have been paid overtime on the basis of 96 hours for l4 days doing the 
same job on same post in Maintenance yard which the Workman Nazir Ahmed was doing at Durg. Collectively 
marked Annexures W-I, No. of these vouchers are |l!. He has also filed and proved information dated 7.2.2025 
obtained through RTI regarding details of Shift in which maintenance has done and time of departure of train as well 
details of working hours in which he was on duty within the period March, 205 to March, 202I. 


I have heard arguments of Learned Counsel for the Workman Union Mr. Arun Patel and Mr. S.K. Gupta for 
Railways. I have gone through the record as well. 


Following issues arise for consideration in the case in hand. 
4. Whether the claim of the Workman Union is barred by res judicata? 


2. Whether the Management is justified in refusing overtime allowance to Workman Najir 
Ahmed who has been working as AC Mechanic/ helper in the Maintenance Roster on the basis of Work 
Hours spend by him and duty which are excess to the ceiling limit of 96 hours in 74 days, is justified in 
law? 


Issue No.  — 


Learned Counsel for Management of Railway have referred to judgment of Hon’ble High Court 
of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur dated 30.07.20i8 in WP(s) No. 4098/208. A photocopy of this judgment is on 
record. 


A perusal of this judgment reveals that, this Writ was filed by Railways through their General 
Manager against order dated 22.08.20l8, passed by the Central Administrative Tribunal in OA No. 
203/00705/206. The respondent workman in the said writ had prayed to quash and set-aside order dated 
03.02.20i6 passed by the Management of Railways and direction to Railways for grant of proper overtime 
allowances with arrears and interest for the half period as he was not relieved their duties even when the train 
had halted. It also comes out from perusal of this judgment that fact in issue before the Central 
Administrative Tribunal and the Writ Petition was different from the case in hand. 


The perusal of other judgment, OA No. 250/20I7 passed by the Central Administrative 
Tribunal in the case of Najir and others V.s. G.M. Northern Railways and others. This case also related 
to over staying on escort duties. Section | of Civil CPC is being reproduced as follows: 


Ll. Res judicata.—No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and 
substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same 
parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a 
Court competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, 
and has been heard and finally decided by such Court. 


Explanation I.—The expression “former suit” shall denote a suit which has been decided prior to 
a suit in question whether or not it was instituted prior thereto. Explanation

II.—For the purposes of this section, the competence of a Court shall be determined irrespective 
of any provisions as to a right of appeal from the decision of such Court. 


Explanation II.—The matter above referred to must in the former suit have been alleged by one 
party and either denied or admitted, expressly or impliedly, by the other. Explanation 


IV.—Any matter which might and ought to have been made ground of defence or attack in such 
former suit shall be deemed to have been a matter directly and substantially in issue in such suit. 


Explanation V.—Any relief claimed in the plaint, which is not expressly granted by the decree, 
shall for the purposes of this section, be deemed to have been refused. 


Explanation VI.—Where persons litigate bona fide in respect of a public right or of a private 
right claimed in common for themselves and others, all persons interested in such right shall, for the 
purposes of this section, be deemed to claim under the persons so litigating . / 


Explanation VII.—The provisions of this section shall apply to a proceeding for the execution of 
a decree and references in this section to any suit, issue or former suit shall be construed as references, 
respectively, to a proceeding for the execution of the decree, question arising in such proceeding and a 
former proceeding for the execution of that decree. 


Explanation VIII. —An issue heard and finally decided by a Court of limited jurisdiction, 
competent to decide such issue, shall operate as res judicata in a subsequent suit, notwithstanding that 
such Court of limited jurisdiction was not competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such 
issue has been subsequently raised 


Since, the facts in issue are not substantially the same, then the case in hand and the referred cases, 
it is held that the claim of the Workman is not barred by res judicata. 


Issue No. 4 is answered accordingly. 
Issue No. 2 - 


The relevant portion of the Railway Board Circular dated 24/25.0.985 is being reproduced as 
follows: 


“Reliving at intermediate stations — 


Whenever possible, the break in duty may be considered at en-route stations having 
resting facilities, after ॥0 to ॥2 hours duty with a fresh state of staff taking over and where this is not 
feasible, the staff should be given adequate compensatory rest at home station to keep this cumulative duty 
hours below permissible limit of /04 hours for 74 days period. 


It also comes out from perusal of this letter that it is with respect to the deployment of AC and 
Electrical staff in the Air condition and power coaches of various trains including Rajdhani, Deluxe and 
other trains. 


This is also not disputed that as per circulars, the duty hours for AC Mechanics/Helpers in the 
Maintenance Hours is 96 hours for 4 days and they will be entitled to overtime allowance as per relevant 
provisions when they work above the ceiling limit. The letter dated 4.05.205 issued by the Assistant 
Personnel Officer, wherein he states that the AC Technical Staff of Durg (AC Technicians/Helpers working 
in the Maintenance Roster) should be 04 hours as instead of 96 hours as per Circular of Railway Board 
dated 24/25.0.985. The relevant portion of this circular has been mentioned earlier, this circular talks only 
with respect to the AC staff in escorting duty and not in maintenance duty. Hence, this letter and this 
interpretation of the Assistant Personnel Officer of the Railways in the Office of South Eastern Railways at 
Raipur made by him in his letter No. E/PS/R/Welfare/TA&OT/0I/204 dated 4.05.205 is nothing but 
misinterpretation of the Railway Board Circular of 24/25.0.985. 


It is relevant to mention on this juncture the fact that, from the RTI document filed from the side of 
Workman Union, the AC Mechanics and Helpers working in the Maintenance Roster in West Central 
Railway at Bhopal are being paid overtime on the basis of 96 Hours work in |4 days, hence on this score 
also the action of Management is discriminatory and arbitrary. 


Hence on the basis of above discussion, the action of Management on the basis of this letter in 
not granting overtime to the AC Mechanic/Helpers working within the Maintenance Roster who have 
worked beyond the ceiling limit of 96 Hours in 4 days is held unjustified in law. 


Issue No. 2 is answered accordingly.

other better scheme of relief the workmen are entitled to?"

is a Workman Union registered and has been authorized by the Union to file the statement of claim in the case as well 
to produce the case vide resolution of Union dated 09.2.202, passed in its General Body meeting, file the statement 
of claim. He has filed list of concerned employees who are covered under the reference, they have been working with 
the Management of Railways since last 0 years and are engaged in the job of cleaning of the railway premises. The 
new Thekedar under whom they are working, which has been made an opposite party, which is CISB Facility 
Services Private Limited has defaulted in payment of their wages. The Union made a complaint in this respect before 
the Authorities that the Contractor has disengaged the members of the Union, list enclosed, without any notice or 
compensation. They are employing other persons in their place. A complaint was made in this respect with Railways. 
The Assistant Divisional Commercial Manager sent a letter to the Contractor on 02.03.202] with regard to revised 
manpower recruitment for the work of cleaning, filed as Annexure-6 to the statement of claim. The Union further 
raised a dispute in this respect which could not be conciliated, hence this reference. 


According to the workman union, the action of contractor in disengaging the Workmen without any notice 
or compensation is unjust, illegal and arbitrary. It has been prayed that holding the action of Contractor in disengaging 
the Workman is unjust and illegal, they have held entitled to be reinstated with back wages and benefits. 


Railways have filed their written statement of defense and have taken a case that, the Union is not a 
registered union. The contract of mechanized cleaning of Railway Station was awarded by Railways to CISB Services 
Pvt. Ltd. They have started their work from 0.07.2020. Railways have denied the case of the Workman Union that 
the Workmen in the case in hand have been working since last 0 years, it is further their case that, the wages of the 
workman are regularly paid and Railways ensured regular and adequate payment of wages being principle employer. 
These workmen are employees of the Contractor; hence Railways did not have any hand in their alleged termination. 


The Contractor did not appear in spite of service of notice. Hence, the case has proceeded ex-parte 
against the Contractor. 


In evidence, the Workman Union has filed affidavits of Narendra Kumar Lahre, Secretary of the Union, 
Workman Pourna Nand, Dilip Kumar Koray, as their examination in chief. They have been cross-examined by 
Management of Railways. The Workman Union has further filed the minutes of meeting of their Union, as well the 
resolution, the registration documents of the Union and Identity Cards issued to the Workman by the Contractor all in 
photocopy. 


Management of Railways has filed affidavit of its witness Avinash Kumar Anand as his examination in 
chief, he has been cross examined by the Union. 


As stated above, the Contractor never appeared nor they filed any written statement of defense. They did not 
appear to cross examine any witness nor did they file any evidence. 


I have heard argument of Learned Counsel for the Workman Union Mr. Anil Dwivedi and Mr. S.K. Gupta 
Learned Counsel for Railways. 


It is further to mention here that Railways has filed Outsourcing Agreement with Contractor, complaints 
made by the Workman Union against the Contractors, attendance sheets of the employees and different applications 
filed by the contractor and workman Union before the Railways with different allegations against the Contractors. 


The reference itself is the issue for determination in the case in hand. 


The first charge of the Workman Union is that, they have not been paid their wages by the contractors. 
They could claim their wages under payment of wages act before Appropriate Authority. If the appropriate Authority 
finds that the workman have not been paid wages as per law, they may pass an order in this respect and also held the 
Railways responsible for payment of wages being principle employer. As regards disengagement of the workmen 
without notice or compensation by the contractor, since the employment of the Workman and continuous employment 
is not disputed, hence, termination without complying with the provisions of Section 25F of the Act is liable to be 
held unjust and illegal. Accordingly, termination of services of the Workman by the Contractor is held unjust in law. 


4428 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 6, 2026/VAISAKHA 26, 948 [PART II—SEC. 3(ii)] 


As regards relief admissible to the Workman, since they are not appointed against any vacancy on regular 
basis rather they are Outsourced employees, a lump sum compensation of Rs. 50,000/- to each of the Workmen in lieu 
of their claims will meet the ends of justice in the case in hand to which they are entitled to recover from the 
Contractor. 


The reference stands answered accordingly. 
AWARD 


Holding the demand of the Railway Station Thekedar Safaikarmi Kalyan Sangh, Chhattisgarh is 
justified & legal in law, they are entitled to a lump sum compensation of Rs. 50,000/- to each of the Workmen in 
lieu of their claims will meet the ends of justice in the case in hand to which they are entitled to recover from the 
Contractor.

As per letter dated ३30/000/2023 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference 
has been made to this Tribunal under Section-l0 of Industrial Disputes Act, 947 (in short the ‘Act’) as per 
Notification No. RP-8(4-06)/2023-ES.III dt. 30/07/2023. The dispute under reference relates to: 


“Whether the action on the part of the management of South Eastern Central Railway Bilaspur (CG) in 
retrenching the workman Shri Yashwant Giri Goswami, S/o Laxmi Giri Goswami, substitute Telephone Attendant 
cum Dak Khalasi, on the basis of purported resignation letter is legal and justified? If not, to what relief, the 
workman is entitled to?” 


The case of the workman is mainly that he was appointed by the Senior Administrative Officer on the post 
of Telephone Attendant-cum-Daak Khalasi in pay matrix level-I, 7" CPC vide order dated 22.04.209 and worked 
continuously till 30.06.202l without any break, his services were terminated by the department under an oral order 
without notice or compensation. He had acquired permanent status of an employee, this action of termination of his 
service by the department is in violation of section 25-F and 25-G of the Act hence, is unjust, illegal and arbitrary. He 
has requested that set aside his termination, he be reinstated with back-wages and benefits. 


The department has taken a case that, the workman was appointed vide letter dated 22.04.209. He 
accepted the terms and conditions of the offer letter and thereafter, Office Order dated 29.04.20l9 was issued, 
appointing him as substitute Telephone Attendant-cum-Daak Khalasi in pay matrix level-I, 77 CPC. He was attached 
with Deputy Chief Engineer and joined under him under para 4 of the Establishment Rule No. 250/200 as Telephone 
Attendant-cum-Daak Khalasi.After joining on 29.04.209, the workman submitted a letter dated 02.05.209 to the 
department stating that he was not willing to work and his services be terminated, this letter was forwarded by Deputy 


[भाग IVS 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 6, 2026/वैशाख 26, 948 443] 


Chief Engineer (General) to Senior Personnel Officer, Headquarter vide his letter dated 06.05.20I9 and after the 
approval of Principal Chief Engineer his services were terminated from 02.05.20l9 vide Office Order dated 
07.06.209. Thus according to management, he submitted his resignation just after four days in service which was 
duly accepted. Hence, according to department, the workman was never disengaged by them rather he himself 
resigned from service. Department has requested that the reference be answered against the workman. 


In his rejoinder, the workman has denied the case of the department that he himself resigned. 


In Evidence, the workman filed his affidavit as his Examination-in-chief, he was cross-examined by the 
department. The department filed affidavit of its witness Snehasish Ghosh as his Examination-in-chief. The 
department filed and proved documents Ex-M/I to M/I0, to be referred to as and when require. 


I have heard argument of Learned Counsel for Workman Mr. Shailesh Mishra and Mr. S.K. Gupta, Learned 
Counsel for Department. The workman side has filed written submission, also which are part of record. I have gone 
through the written submission and record as well. 


On perusal of record in light of rival arguments, the sole issue which arises for determination is. 


Whether the services of the workman stood terminated on the basis of his resignation letter dated 
02.05.209 and order passed by the Officers of Department on this letter accepting his resignation? 


In his statement, the workman has denied that he filed any resignation letter. He denied his signature on the 
resignation letter. The management witness has proved this resignation letter. In these circumstances, the burden was 
on the workman to prove by evidence of forgery that his signatures on his resignation dated 02.05.209 are in fact not 
done by him. He has not discharged his burden. Hence, the fact that he filed his resignation letter as stated above is 
held proved. 


Learned Counsel for the workman has also submitted that, even if the workman had filed his resignation 
letter but, termination of his services could not be held complete till its acceptance of resignation letter and order with 
respect to dismissal of service was communicated to him. He has referred to Judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court in 
the case of, State of Punjab vs Amar Singh Harika, 7966 SCC Online SC 48, in the case referred, the employee was 
found guilty of misconduct in a departmental enquiry, he was sent a communication by the department to the effect 
that in light of finding of enquiry holding him guilty, he could exercise his option to resign. Pursuant to that letter the 
employee sent his resignation. Order of dismissal was passed on the resignation. The question which was before the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court was whether the order of dismissal on the basis of his resignation letter would be effective 
from the date of communication or from the date of order. The Five Judges Bench of Hon’ble Supreme Court held 
that, it would be effective from the date of its communication or its publication. 


Learned Counsel for workman has submitted that since, this order was never communicated to him or 
published, it could not be held effective. Office memorandum dated 07.06.20l9 which declares that service of the 
workman shall stand terminated from the date of his resignation letter dated 02.05.209 and a copy was ordered to be 
sent to the workman along with other offices including Pay and Accounts Office, in such circumstances, it cannot be 
said that the order was not published, may be, it may not served on him. 


Even otherwise, though the case of the workman was that he worked till 202, but he could not produce any 
evidence to support his this claim that he worked for 240 days in any year, but he could at least produce his pay slips 
or attendance slips to corroborate his this case, in absence of such evidence, his case that he worked for 240 days in a 
year also held not proved. 


“In light of above discussion, holding the termination of services of the workman by Department, just and 
legal, the workman is held entitled to no relief.” 


The reference stands answered accordingly. 
No order as to cost.

As per letter dated 24/05/207 by the Government of India, Ministry of Labour, New Delhi, the reference is 
made to this Tribunal under Section-l0 of Industrial Disputes Act, |947 (in short the ‘Act’)as per Notification 
No. L-20/30/206 (IR(B-D) dt. 24/05/207. The dispute under reference relates to: 


"Whether the demand of Union claiming difference of wages in favour of Sh. Radheshyam Rathore daily 
wage employee from 6.05.83 to 05.07.44 is justified or not? If so, what relief the daily wager is entitled 
for?" 


Case of the Workman Union is that, the Workman Radheyshyam Rathore was appointed as a peon on 
temporary basis by the then State Bank of Indore in its Sarangpur Branch on scale wage Rs. 245 with DA from the 
period 6.05.983 to 23.05.983 and 07..983 to 2..983. Thereafter he was appointed as daily wager on 
8.08.986 on a daily wage under oral orders of the Branch Manager and worked till 05.0.20l! when he was 
terminated without any notice or compensation for which he has filed another case. His claim in the case in hand is 
that he is entitled to the wages paid to the temporary staff of the Bank discharging the same duties of the Peon but he 
was paid only wages on Collector Rate, which is unjust and illegal, the Union has prayed that the Workman be paid 
its all wages accordingly. 


Case of the Management is that the Workman was appointed for total period of about 2 weeks, on a leave 
vacancy for which he was paid scale wages. Thereafter, he worked as a daily wager for which he was paid wages on 
Collector Rates. It is further the case of the Management that the scale wages according to bi partite settlement are 
admissible to the Regularly Appointed staff and not to the daily wager. 


Both the parties have filed their affidavits. They have cross-examined by their adversaries. They have filed 
some certain documents which were referred to as and when require. 


I have heard argument of Learned Counsel Mr. Arun Patel for the Workman and Mr. Pranay Choubey for 
the Management Bank and have gone through the record. 


The reference itself is the issue for determination in the case in hand. 


[भाग aves 3(ii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 6, 2026/वैशाख 26, 948 4433 


The main question involve for consideration is whether the bi-partite settlement applies to the daily wager 
also or not. The workman side could not cite any provisions in the bi partite settlement in this respect. It also comes 
out from perusal of the bi partite settlement that, it is applicable to the staff who are on regular appointment may be as 
a permanent or a temporary workers. Hence, the claim of the Workman with respect to the period in which he has 
worked as a daily wager with the Bank is not admissible in law with regard to parity to the wages paid to the regular 
employees. 


With regard to period he was appointed on temporary basis on leave vacancy, was for two times as 
mentioned in his statement of claim. The workman side itself admits that he was paid scale wage for this period. 


In the light of above discussion and evidence the reference is answered as follows. 
AWARD 


Holding the demand of Union claiming difference of wages in favour of Sh. Radheshyam Rathore daily 
wage employee from 76.05.63 to 05.07.474 is unjustified and against law. The Workman is entitled to no relief. 


No order as to cost.

ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA 
ORDER 
New Delhi, the Ist January, 2026 


O.N. 5.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Rajasthan, 2023 for 141-Ahore 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No.464/RJ-LA/2023, 
dated 30" October, 2023; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election Officer 
an account of his election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him or his election agent under Section 
77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 141-Ahore Assembly Constituency of 
Rajasthan, 2023 was declared by the Returning Officer on 37 December, 2023 and hence the last date for lodging the 
account of Election Expenses was 2™ January, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Jalore report dated 09.01.2024 forwarded by the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Rajasthan vide his letter no. F.3(1)(5)EEM/ELECTION/Candidates’ Exp. /433 dated 16.01.2024, under 
sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Masara Ram a contesting candidate from 141- 
Ahore Assembly Constituency of state of Rajasthan has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under 
law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Jalore a Show-Cause notice No. 
76/RJ-LA/141/2023/CEMS-I, dated 107" July, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Masara Ram for not lodging of account of Election 
Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Masara Ram was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining 
the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District Election Officer, 
Jalore within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Jalore vide his letter no. P. (1) (1) L-A.Ele./Exp. Mo./2024/3050 
dated 22.11.2024 has informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Masara Ram, on dated 
12.11.2024; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Jalore in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. P. (1) 
(1) L.A.Ele./Exp. Mo./2024/3054 dated 16.12.2024 has reported that Sh. Masara Ram has not submitted account of 
election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Masara Ram has neither furnished any reason nor 
explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as 
prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified 


, 


and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


16 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : MAY 16, 2026/V AISAKHA 26, 1948 [PART II—SEC. 3(iii)] 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Masara 
Ram has failed to lodge account of election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; 
and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Masara Ram, residence of Sanvara, Tehsil-Ahore, District- 
Jalore, Rajasthan, a contesting candidate from 141-Ahore Assembly Constituency of Rajasthan in General 
Election to Legislative Assembly, 2023 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House 
of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of 
three years from the date of this order. 


[F. No. 76/RJ-LA/141/2023/CEMS-I] 
By Order, 
RAKESH KUMAR, Secy.

WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 03- Khadoor Sahib Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 047 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 04.07.2024 of DEO, Tarn Taran under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Sh. Sarabjit Singh, a contesting candidate from 03- Khadoor Sahib Parliamentary 
Constituency of state of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/PB- 
LS/3/2024/CEMS-I, dated 317 January, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Sarabjit Singh, for not lodging of the account of Election 
Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Sarabjit Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Tarn Taran District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Tarn Taran has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Smt. 
Jasbir Kaur (Mother of Sh. Sarabjit Singh) on 21.11.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Tarn Taran in his Supplementary Report, received through the 
CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2026/R-1265, dated 17.02.2026 has reported that Sh. Sarabjit Singh has not 
submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. 
Sarabjit Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or 
under this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Sarabjit Singh 
has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; 
and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the

Punjab, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the 
Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date 
of this order.

LS/3/2024/CEMS-I, dated 317 January, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Sarabjit Singh, for not lodging of the account of Election 
Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Sarabjit Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Tarn Taran District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and

Jasbir Kaur (Mother of Sh. Sarabjit Singh) on 21.11.2025; and

submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. 
Sarabjit Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or

the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 17th November, 2025 


O.N. 14.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Assam, 2024, for 02- Dhubri Parliamentary 
Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/EPS/2024(3), 
dated 12" April, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 02- Dhubri Parliamentary Constituency of Assam, 2024 was 
declared by the Returning Officer on 047 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 16.08.2024 of DEO, Dhubri under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/496, dated 21.08.2024 
stating that Sh. Shukur Ali, a contesting candidate from 02- Dhubri Parliamentary Constituency of state of Assam 
has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 
76/AS-LS/02/2024/CEMS-I, dated 307 December, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Shukur Ali, for not lodging of the account of 
Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Shukur Ali was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining 
the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Dhubri District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Dhubri has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Ashaful 
(Brother of Shukur Ali) on 15.01.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Dhubri in his Supplementary Report, received through the CEO, 
Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/Vol-I/19, dated 20.09.2025 has reported that Sh. Shukur Ali has not 
submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, 
Sh. Shukur Ali has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person Shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Shukur Ali has 
failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and

Parliamentary Constituency of state of Assam, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either 
House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a 
period of three years from the date of this order.

O.N. 15.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Assam, 2024, for 02- Dhubri Parliamentary 
Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/EPS/2024(3), dated 
12" April, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 02- Dhubri Parliamentary Constituency of Assam, 2024 was 
declared by the Returning Officer on 047 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 16.08.2024 of DEO, Dhubri under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/496, dated 21.08.2024 
stating that Sh. Alakesh Roy, a contesting candidate from 02- Dhubri Parliamentary Constituency of state of Assam 
has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ 
No. 76/AS-LS/02/2024/CEMS-I, dated 307 December, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct 
of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Alakesh Roy, for not lodging of the account of 
Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Alakesh Roy was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Dhubri District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and

WHEREAS, the DEO, Dhubri has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Alakesh 
Roy on 10.01.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Dhubri in his Supplementary Report, received through the CEO, 
Assam vide his letter no. ELE.64/2023/Vol-I/19, dated 20.09.2025 has reported that Sh. Alakesh Roy has not 
submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. 
Alakesh Roy has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to 
lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Alakesh Roy has 
failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Alakesh Roy, resident of Vill- Uttar Raipur Pt.II, P.O. 
Moterjhar, P.S. Golakganj, Dist. Dhubri, Assam, Pin-783334 and a contesting candidate from 02- Dhubri 
Parliamentary Constituency of state of Assam, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either 
House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a 
period of three years from the date of this order. 


[F. No. 76/AS-LS/02/2024/CEMS-I]

दिनांक 16.08.2024 की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, सुश्री राधारानी विश्वास, जो असम के 02-धुबरी संसदीय निर्वाचन क्षेत्र से

उप-नियम (6) के अंतर्गत, सुश्री राधारानी विश्वास को लेखा दाखिल न किए जाने संबंधी कारणों को स्पष्ट करते हुए 
आयोग को अपना अभ्यावेदन लिखित रूप में प्रस्तुत करने और नोटिस के प्राप्त होने की तारीख से 20 दिनों के भीतर जिला

यत:, मुख्य निर्वाचन अधिकारी, असम से उनके दिनांक 20.09.2025 के पत्र सं. 5/ 5.64/2023/४0-॥19, के 
तहत प्राप्त जिला निर्वाचन अधिकारी, धुबरी की अनुपूरक रिपोर्ट के द्वारा सूचित किया है कि सुश्री राधारानी विश्वास ने 
निर्वाचन व्यय के लेखे का कोई विवरण प्रस्तुत नहीं किया है। इसके अतिरिक्त, उक्त नोटिस मिलने के उपरांत, 
सुश्री राधारानी विश्वास द्वारा विधि के अंतर्गत यथा-विहित लेखे दाखिल करने में अपनी असफलता के लिए भारत निर्वाचन 
आयोग को न तो कोई कारण बताया है और न ही कोई स्पष्टीकरण दिया है; और 


यत:, लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 की धारा 10क में यह उपबंधित किया गया है कि:- 
“यदि निवाचिित आयोग का सयाधान हो जाता है कि कोई व्यक्ति-

है, दाखिल करने यें असफल CET है; तथा 
(व) उस असफलता के लिए कोई अच्छा कारण या न्यायोचित्य नहीं रखता है; 


तो निर्वाचन आयोग शासकीय राजपत्र में प्रकाशित आदेश द्वारा उसको PAST घोषित करेगा और ऐसा व्यक्ति उस 
आदेश की तारीख से तीन वर्ष की कालावधि के लिए freer होया। 


यत:, तथ्यों और उपलब्ध रिकार्डों के आधार पर, आयोग का यह समाधान हो गया है कि सुश्री राधारानी विश्वास 
अपने निर्वाचन व्यय के लेखे दाखिल करने में असफल रही हैं और उनके पास ऐसा करने में असफल रहने के लिए कोई भी 
उचित कारण अथवा औचित्य नहीं है; और 
अत:, अब, लोक प्रतिनिधित्व अधिनियम, 1951 की धारा 10क के अनुसरण में, भारत निर्वाचन आयोग एतद्दारा

इस आदेश की तारीख से तीन वर्ष की अवधि के लिए संसद के किसी भी सदन अथवा राज्य अथवा संघ राज्य क्षेत्र की

New Delhi, the 17th November, 2025 


O.N. 17.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Punjab, 2024, for 06- Anandpur Sahib 
Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification 
No. 464/EPS/2024(7), dated 7 May, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 

WHEREAS, the result of the election for 06- Anandpur Sahib Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 04" June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 

WHEREAS, as per the report dated 05.07.2024 of DEO, Rupnagar under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Sh. Satpal, a contesting candidate from 06-Anandpur Sahib Parliamentary Constituency of 
state of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 

WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/PB- 
LS/06/2024/CEMS-I, dated 31 January, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Satpal, for not lodging of the account of Election Expenses; 
and 

WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Satpal was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining the 
reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the District Election 
Officer, Rupnagar District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 

WHEREAS, the DEO, Rupnagar has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Satpal 
on 03.02.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rupnagar in his Supplementary Report no. Elec.2025/783; dated 
14.08.2025 has reported that Sh. Satpal has not submitted any representation or statement of account of election 
expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Satpal has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“Tf the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure,

the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Satpal has failed 
to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Satpal, resident of Vill- Chankoi, P.O. Gulpur, Tehsil 
Balachaur, Dist. SBS Nagar/Nawanshahr, Punjab and a contesting candidate from 06- Anandpur Sahib 
Parliamentary Constituency of State of Punjab, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 20th November, 2025 


O.N. 19.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Punjab, 2024, for 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary 
Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/EPS/2024(7), 
dated 77 May, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 was 
declared by the Returning Officer on 04" June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 05.07.2024 of DEO, Ludhiana under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran, a contesting candidate from 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary 
Constituency of state of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/PB- 
LS/07/2024/CEMS-I, dated 06" February, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran, for not lodging of the account 
of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran was directed to submit representation in writing to the 
Commission explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses 
with the District Election Officer, Ludhiana District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Ludhiana has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Amritpal 
Singh Chhandran on 13.02.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Ludhiana in his Supplementary Report, received through the CEO, 
Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2025/R-1601, dated 07.04.2025 has reported that Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran has 
not submitted any representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, 
Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of 
India for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 
person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.’’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Amritpal Singh 
Chhandran has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the 
failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Amritpal Singh Chhandran, resident of H.No. 613, Azad Nagar, 
Patiala, Punjab, Pin-147001 and a contesting candidate from 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary Constituency of State of 
Punjab, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the Parliament or the 
Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three years from the date 
of this order.

May, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an

WHEREAS, the result of the election for 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary Constituency of Punjab, 2024 was

Expenses was 4" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 04.07.2024 of DEO, Ludhiana under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the CEO, Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2024/R-7458, dated 
22.07.2024 stating that Sh. Chandi, a contesting candidate from 07- Ludhiana Parliamentary Constituency of state 
of Punjab has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, a ‘Show-Cause Notice’ No. 76/PB- 
LS/07/2024/CEMS-I, dated 06" February, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections 
Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Chandi, for not lodging of the account of Election Expenses; 
and 


WHEREAS, through the above said ‘Show Cause Notice’ and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Chandi was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission explaining the 
reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the District Election 
Officer, Ludhiana District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the DEO, Ludhiana has reported that the said ‘Show Cause Notice’ was served to Sh. Chandi

Punjab vide his letter no. Elec-2025/R-1601, dated 07.04.2025 has reported that Sh. Chandi has not submitted any 
representation or statement of account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Chandi has 
neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to lodge the account of 
his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:-

“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person-

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 21st November, 2025 


O.N. 22.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Haryana, 2024 for 10-Faridabad 
Parliamentary Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. O.N. 114(E), 
dated 29" April, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election for 10-Faridabad Parliamentary Constituency of 
Haryana, 2024 was declared by the Returning Officer on 47 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the 
account of Election Expenses was 47 July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Faridabad dated 30.07.2024 forwarded by the Chief 
Electoral Officer, Haryana vide his letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GEL-2024/2AE-7497, dated 05.08.2024, under sub-rule (1) 
of Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla a contesting candidate from 10- 
Faridabad Parliamentary Constituency of state of Haryana has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as 
required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Faridabad a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/HR-LS/10/2024/CEMS-I, dated 207 December, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla for not lodging 
of his account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Faridabad within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Faridabad vide his letter no. Election-2025/229 dated 05.02.2025 
has informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla on 04.01.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Faridabad in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Election- 
2025/663 dated 07.04.2025 has reported that Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla has not submitted account of election 
expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla has neither furnished any reason nor 
explanation to the Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as 
prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(iii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 16, 2026/वैशाख 26, 1948 57 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the Election 
Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Gyan Chand Bainsla, Near Sarkari School, Kamrawali, Barauli(149) 
Baroli, Palwal, Haryana-121102, a contesting candidate for 10-Faridabad Parliamentary Constituency of 
Haryana in General Election to Lok Sabha, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order.

New Delhi, the 24th November, 2025 


O.N. 26.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Lok Sabha of Kerala, 2024 for 10-Thrissur Parliamentary 
Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. O.N. 92(E), dated 
28" March, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be a true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the election for 10-Thrissur Parliamentary Constituency of Kerala, 2024 was 
declared by the Returning Officer on 047 June, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of Election 
Expenses was 04" July, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report dated 05.07.2024 of District Election Officer, Thrissur under sub-rule (1) of 
Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 received through the Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala vide his letter 
no. EL1/113/2024-ELEC; dated 31.07.2024 stating that Sh. M. S. Jafarghan, a contesting candidate from 
10-Thrissur Parliamentary Constituency in General Election to Lok Sabha of Kerala, 2024, has failed to lodge the 
account of his election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Thrissur a Show-Cause Notice no. 
76/KL-PC/2024/CEMS-II, dated 29" August, 2024 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. M. S. Jafarghan, for not lodging of the account of 
Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. M. S. Jafarghan was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge the account of his election expenses with the 
District Election Officer, Thrissur District within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Thrissur through Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala in his report no. 
EL1/113/2024-ELEC; dated 21.01.2025 has reported that the said Show Cause Notice was Served to 
Sh. M. S. Jafarghan on 09.09.2024; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Thrissur in his Supplementary Report dated 05.10.2024 and 
26.09.2025 on account of the candidate received through Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala letter no. EL1/113/2024- 
ELEC; dated 21.01.2025 and 08.10.2025 has reported that Sh. M. S. Jafarghan has not submitted any representation 
or statement of the account of election expenses. Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. M. S. Jafarghan has 
neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the Election Commission of India for failure to lodge the account of 
his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that: - 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 
(e) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses within the time and in the manner required by or under this 
Act, and 
(f) has no good reason or justification for the failure, 


the Election Commission shall, by order published in the Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such 


, 


person shall be disqualified for a period of three years from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on basis of the facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. M. S. Jafarghan 
has failed to lodge the account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; 
and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. M. S. Jafarghan, resident of Munnakkaparambil House, 
Ponjanam P O, Kattoor, Thrissur, Pin-680702 and a contesting candidate from 10-Thrissur Parliamentary 
Constituency of Kerala in General Election to the Lok Sabha, 2024, to be disqualified for being chosen as and for 
being a member of either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or 
Union Territory for a period of three years from the date of this order.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 27th November, 2025 


O.N. 29.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 73-Kosli 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/ECI/HAR- 
LA/2024, dated 5° September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana, 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Rewari forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana 
vide his letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of Rule 89 
of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Lavinder Singh a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly 
Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Rewari a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Lavinder Singh for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Lavinder Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Rewari within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari vide his letter no. Elec-2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Lavinder Singh on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Lavinder Singh has not submitted account of election expenses. 
Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Lavinder Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’;

WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Lavinder Singh 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Lavinder Singh, House No. 985, Village Kanwali, District 
Rewari, Haryana, a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana in General Election to 
Legislative Assembly, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of either House of the 
Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory for a period of three 
years from the date of this order.

ORDER 
New Delhi, the 27th November, 2025 


O.N. 30.—WHEREAS, the General Election to Legislative Assembly of Haryana, 2024 for 73-Kosli 
Assembly Constituency was held in pursuance of the Election Commission of India Notification No. 464/ECI/HAR- 
LA/2024, dated 5h September, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per Section 78 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, every contesting candidate at an 
election shall, within 30 days from the date of election of the returned candidate, lodge with the District Election 
Officer an account of his/her election expenses which shall be true copy of the account kept by him/her or his/her 
election agent under Section 77 of the said act; and 


WHEREAS, the result of the above-mentioned election from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana, 
was declared by the Returning Officer on 8" October, 2024 and hence the last date for lodging the account of 
Election Expenses was 77 November, 2024; and 


WHEREAS, as per the report submitted by DEO, Rewari forwarded by the Chief Electoral Officer, 
Haryana vide his letter no. 6/Elect-Exp./GELA-HR-2024/Elec-2025/2AE-692 dated 05.02.2025, under sub-rule (1) of 
Rule 89 of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Naval Singh a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly 
Constituency has failed to lodge account of election expenses, as required under law; and 


WHEREAS, on the basis of the said report of the District Election Officer, Rewari a Show-Cause notice 
No. 76/HR-LA/Exp. Account/2024/CEMS-I, dated 30" April, 2025 was issued under sub rule (5) of Rule 89 of the 
Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 by the Election Commission of India to Sh. Naval Singh for not lodging of his 
account of Election Expenses; and 


[भाग 1---खण्ड 3(iii)] भारत का राजपत्र : मई 16, 2026/वैशाख 26, 1948 प्रा 


WHEREAS, through the above said Show Cause Notice and under sub rule (6) of Rule 89 of the Conduct of 
Elections Rules, 1961, Sh. Naval Singh was directed to submit representation in writing to the Commission 
explaining the reasons for not lodging the account and also to lodge account of election expenses with the District 
Election Officer, Rewari within 20 days from the date of receipt of the notice; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari vide his letter no. Elec-2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has 
informed that the notice was duly served and received by Sh. Naval Singh on 20.05.2025; and 


WHEREAS, the District Election Officer, Rewari in his Supplementary Report, vide its letter no. Elec- 
2025/711 dated 16.06.2025 has reported that Sh. Naval Singh has not submitted account of election expenses. 
Further, after receipt of the said notice, Sh. Naval Singh has neither furnished any reason nor explanation to the 
Election Commission of India, for failure to lodge the account of his election expenses as prescribed under law; and 


WHEREAS, Section 10 A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides that:- 
“If the Election Commission is satisfied that a person- 


(a) has failed to lodge an account of election expenses, within the time and in the manner required by or under 
this Act, and 


(b) has no good reason or justification for the failure, the Election Commission shall, by order published in the 
Official Gazette, declare him to be disqualified and any such person shall be disqualified for a period of three years 
from the date of the order.”’; 


WHEREAS, on the basis of facts and available records, the Commission is satisfied that Sh. Naval Singh 
has failed to lodge account of his election expenses and has no good reason or justification for the failure to do so; and 


NOW, THEREFORE, in pursuance of Section 10A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, the 
Election Commission of India hereby declares Sh. Naval Singh, House No. 89, Village Mandiya Khurd, Tehsil 
and District Rewari, Haryana, a contesting candidate from 73-Kosli Assembly Constituency of Haryana in 
General Election to Legislative Assembly, 2024 to be disqualified for being chosen as and for being a member of 
either House of the Parliament or the Legislative Assembly or the Legislative Council of a State or Union Territory 
for a period of three years from the date of this order. 


[F. No. 76/HR-LA/73/2024/CEMS-I] 
By Order, 
RAKESH KUMAR, Secy.
